observation.visible_scene: Close-up of the front wheel of a white car (silver five-spoke alloy rim with a center logo, black tire showing raised "TR" sidewall lettering, black mud flap behind it) on a dark speckled surface. A hand holding a black pressure-washer spray gun is directed at the wheel, emitting a fan-shaped water jet with visible mist and droplets.
visible_changes: The water jet enters from the lower-right at the start and is swept upward along the right side of the rim, then tracked across the upper-right and finally to the top edge of the tire as the clip progresses.

The black spray gun and the gripping hand appear from the right edge of the frame (the gun body is not visible in the first few frames, only the jet) and move progressively upward as the jet follows the wheel.
The rim's spoke orientation, center logo, and the "TR" lettering stay in the same angular position in every frame, so the wheel is not rotating; only the gun and jet move relative to it.
Wet sheen, spray mist, and droplets are visible on the tire and rim, with water running off the tire surface.
The white body panel, black mud flap, and ground stay in fixed screen positions, indicating the camera is essentially static while the spraying action moves.
outside_clip_unknowns: The operator's body and the rest of the vehicle are never shown.
What precedes the first frame (the gun is partly off-screen at the start) and what follows the last frame are not visible.
The source of the water and the overall cleaning outcome are unseen.
uncertain_details: Whether the gun/hand were already present before the first sampled frame, since only the jet is clearly visible at t=0.
Exact nozzle-to-wheel distance and spray pressure cannot be measured.
Any very slight camera drift is indistinguishable from the moving spray.
